title: Coxeter presentation from two-letter deletion for involution words
statement:
Let $G$ be a set with an associative multiplication, an identity $1$, and two-sided inverses, and let $I$ be a finite set [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set], and let $i\mapsto t_i$ be an injective map $I	o G$ with $t_i
e1$ and $t_i^2=1$, whose image generates $G$. For $g\in G$ let $\ell(g)$ be the minimum length of a word in the $t_i$ representing $g$, with the empty word representing $1$. Assume the two-letter deletion condition: whenever $t_{i_1}\cdots t_{i_k}=g$ and $k>\ell(g)$, there are $1\le a<b\le k$ such that deleting precisely the letters in positions $a,b$ gives another word for $g$. For $i
e j$ assume $t_it_j$ has finite order $m_{ij}$. Let $F(I)$ be the free group of words in $x_i^{\pm1}$ modulo adjacent inverse cancellation, and let $\pi:F(I)	o G$ send $x_i$ to $t_i$. Then $\ker\pi$ is the normal subgroup generated by $x_i^2$ and $(x_ix_j)^{m_{ij}}$ for $i
e j$; normal generation means the set of finite products of conjugates of these words and their inverses. The empty set $I$ is allowed.

source.place: Chapter IV, §1.5, Theorem 1, deletion/exchange characterization of Coxeter systems. WANTED local copy. Verified online in Mühlherr–Weiss, Coxeter’s enumeration of Coxeter groups, §6, Theorem 6.2(D), https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms.70379; see also Milne Appendix C.11, printed p.610 for its root-system application. No Stacks tag states this abstract group criterion.

proof.text: Let $N$ be the stated set of products of conjugates of relators and their inverses. Concatenation, reversal/inversion and conjugation of such products show directly that $N$ is a normal subgroup. Every relator evaluates to $1$ in $G$, hence $N\subseteq\ker\pi$. Write $U\sim V$ for $UV^{-1}\in N$; normality makes this relation stable under concatenating any fixed words on either side. Modulo $N$, $x_i^{-1}=x_i$ because $x_i^2\in N$, so any signed free word can be replaced by a positive word. A braid move interchanges the alternating length-$m_{ij}$ blocks starting in $i$ and $j$. If these positive blocks are $B_i,B_j$, replace the inverse letters in $B_iB_j^{-1}$ by positive letters. The result is the alternating word $(x_ix_j)^{m_{ij}}$: for even $m_{ij}$ the reversed second block ends the first block with the opposite letter, and the same is true for odd $m_{ij}$. Therefore $B_i\sim B_j$. Deleting an adjacent repeated letter also preserves $\sim$, since its two-letter block is $x_i^2$.

proof.text: We prove by strong induction on $n$ that any two reduced positive words $U,V$ of length $n$ for the same $g$ are connected by braid moves. For $n=0$ both words are empty. For $n>0$ write $U=iU'$, $V=jV'$. Their tails are reduced: shortening a tail would shorten the whole word. If $i=j$, cancel $t_i$ and use induction on the tails of length $n-1$. If $i\ne j$, the tails show $\ell(t_ig)=\ell(t_jg)=n-1$. Apply [lem-sfb-involution-two-descent-prefix] to this pair, whose product has finite order by hypothesis. Choose a reduced word $C$ for its $h$. The lemma gives reduced words $A_iC,A_jC$ of length $n$ for $g$. Cancel the common initial $i$ in $U$ and $A_iC$; their remaining words are reduced of length $n-1$ for $t_ig$, so induction connects them by braid moves. Keeping that initial $i$ fixed connects $U$ to $A_iC$. The identical argument with $j$ connects $V$ to $A_jC$. One braid move connects $A_iC$ and $A_jC$, completing the induction. This proves word comparison without assuming any Coxeter presentation.

proof.text: Next every positive word is $\sim$-equivalent to a reduced positive word with the same product. Induct on its number of letters, writing a nonempty word as $iV$. By induction reduce $V$ to a reduced $R$ of length $r$, and put $v=t_R$. If $iR$ is reduced, stop. Otherwise deletion applied to its $r+1$ letters yields a word for $t_iv$ of length $r-1$. Conversely $v=t_i(t_iv)$ implies $r\le1+\ell(t_iv)$, so $\ell(t_iv)=r-1$. Choose a reduced word $Q$ for $t_iv$. The word $iQ$ represents $v$ and has length $r$, hence is reduced. The preceding reduced-word comparison connects $R$ and $iQ$ by braid moves, so $iR\sim iiQ\sim Q$. The empty word is the induction base. The comparison theorem used here was proved in step 2 from [lem-sfb-involution-two-descent-prefix]; no arbitrary two-letter deletion is being treated as a permitted relator move.

source.place: Agent word argument for Bourbaki IV §1.5 Theorem 1; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Take $f\in\ker\pi$ and choose a finite signed word representing it. Step 1 replaces inverse letters by positive letters modulo $N$, without changing its image in $G$. Step 3 then replaces that word modulo $N$ by a reduced word for $1$. Its length is $\ell(1)=0$, since the empty word represents $1$; it is therefore empty. Thus $f\in N$, proving the reverse inclusion. Together with step 1 this proves the exact claimed normal generation. For $I=\varnothing$, generation makes $G$ trivial, and the free group has only the empty word, so both sides of the kernel equality are the trivial subgroup. For a singleton, no rank-two step is needed: reduced words with distinct initial letters never occur, and the reduction uses only $x_i^2$.
